articles.title: US Open accused of 'corruption' after handing Venus Williams a wild card
articles.standfirst: The seven-time Grand Slam champion's place in the New York draw has sparked criticism over whether reputation is outweighing merit
articles.summary: The seven-time Grand Slam champion's place in the New York draw has sparked criticism over whether reputation is outweighing merit
articles.body:
Venus Williams ' return to the US Open has triggered a fierce debate after the 46-year-old received a wild card into the women's singles draw, with one tennis insider going as far as describing the decision as "corrupt."

Williams remains one of the most recognizable players in the history of the sport, but her ranking and limited recent match activity meant she needed an invitation from organizers to compete in New York.

The USTA ultimately gave her one, allowing the two-time US Open champion to return to a tournament where she first reached the final in 1997.

However, the decision has reopened a wider argument about how Grand Slam wild cards are distributed and whether younger players with stronger recent results are being denied opportunities because tournaments prefer famous names.

US Open wild card decision comes under fire

The criticism centers less on Williams personally than on the system used to award discretionary places in major tournaments.

One tennis insider argued that the process has become too dependent on profile, marketability and relationships rather than current sporting merit, describing the situation as "corrupt."

That is a serious accusation, although there is no suggestion that the US Open broke any formal rule by selecting Williams . Tournament organizers are allowed to award wild cards at their discretion, and former champions have routinely benefited from that flexibility.

Williams also brings obvious commercial appeal, particularly in New York, where she and sister Serena Williams became central figures in one of tennis' most successful eras.

Debate goes beyond Venus Williams

The uncomfortable question is whether that history should continue carrying more weight than the current form of players trying to establish themselves.

Wild cards can provide vital opportunities for young Americans, returning players and competitors whose rankings don't reflect their ability because of injury. Every place given to an established star therefore means one fewer opening for somebody else.

Williams ' record makes her case more compelling than most. She has won seven Grand Slam singles titles, including the US Open in 2000 and 2001, and remains one of the sport's defining figures.

Still, critics argue that prestige shouldn't make wild cards automatic indefinitely.

The controversy has therefore become bigger than one veteran receiving one invitation.

Williams will attract enormous attention when she returns to Flushing Meadows, which is precisely why the US Open wanted her there.

Whether that makes the decision commercially sensible or competitively unfair depends on what fans believe a wild card is supposed to reward.

articles.title: US Open 2026 schedule: Dates, times and where to watch the Grand Slam from New York
articles.standfirst: The final Grand Slam of the season begins August 30, with two weeks of singles action leading to the men's final on September 13
articles.summary: The final Grand Slam of the season begins August 30, with two weeks of singles action leading to the men's final on September 13
articles.body:
The 2026 US Open will bring another packed fortnight of Grand Slam tennis to New York , with the main draw running from Sunday, August 30 through Sunday, September 13 at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center.

First round matches begin on August 30 and continue through September 1, with day sessions starting at 11 a.m. ET and night sessions generally beginning at 7 p.m. ET.

The second round follows on September 2 and 3, before the third-round matches take place on September 4 and 5. The round of 16 is scheduled across September 6 and 7.

Quarterfinals then begin on September 8 as the tournament moves toward its championship weekend.

When are the 2026 US Open finals?

The women's semifinals are scheduled for Thursday, September 10, beginning at 7 p.m. ET.

The men's semifinals take place the following day, with the first scheduled for 3 p.m. ET and the second beginning at 7 p.m. ET.

The women's singles final will be played on Saturday, September 12 at 4 p.m. ET, before the men's championship match brings the tournament to a close on Sunday, September 13 at 2 p.m. ET.

Exact match times during earlier rounds can change once the daily order of play is released.

Where can you watch the 2026 US Open?

ESPN remains the exclusive US broadcaster for the US Open under its long-term agreement with the USTA.

Television coverage will be spread across ESPN, ESPN2 and ABC, while ESPN's digital platforms will provide extensive streaming throughout the tournament.

Beginning in 2026, ESPN's expanded agreement also brings additional US Open streaming coverage, with every match and court available through the ESPN App for eligible subscribers.

ESPN Deportes provides Spanish language coverage in the United States, while TSN and RDS continue carrying the tournament in Canada.

The 2026 tournament begins with three days of first round singles matches before progressing toward championship weekend.

Day sessions during the opening week generally start at 11 a.m. ET, while the main night sessions begin around 7 p.m. ET at Arthur Ashe Stadium.

That gives fans nearly two full weeks of action before the champions are crowned.

The key dates are September 12 for the women's final and September 13 for the men's final, with New York once again providing the stage for the final Grand Slam titles of the season.

articles.title: 'Actually scandalous': US Open ticket prices skyrocket, leaving fans fuming over seatless passes
articles.standfirst: The cost of watching tennis in New York has surged, leaving ordinary fans questioning whether the Grand Slam is becoming a luxury event
articles.summary: The cost of watching tennis in New York has surged, leaving ordinary fans questioning whether the Grand Slam is becoming a luxury event
articles.body:
The US Open is almost here, and while anticipation is building for tennis’ final Grand Slam of the year, fans are facing an unwelcome hurdle: eye-watering ticket prices.

The 2026 tournament officially gets underway with Fan Week on August 23, while the singles main draw begins August 30 at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in Flushing Meadows. The event runs through September 13.

With stars including Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka expected in New York, demand is high. But according to figures circulating this week, the average resale price for entry has climbed significantly compared with the same point last year.

A particularly striking example is the reported $363 price for a grounds pass on the tournament’s opening day. That’s a steep amount for a ticket that doesn’t guarantee a seat inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.

Officially, grounds admission provides first-come, first-served access to general-admission areas in Louis Armstrong Stadium, the Grandstand and the outer courts.

It doesn’t include access to Arthur Ashe, meaning buyers could spend hundreds of dollars without having a reserved seat for the tournament’s biggest matches.

The USTA has also increased the face value of a grounds pass from $60 to $65 this year, although resale demand has pushed some tickets dramatically higher.

Fans question whether the Open is becoming too exclusive

The price gap with other Grand Slam events has fueled even more frustration.

A grounds pass at Wimbledon during the opening week was reportedly around $44.70, while Roland Garros admission was roughly $45. Tickets for the 2027 Australian Open have also been reported at around $35.

Fans have taken to social media to criticize what they see as an increasingly inaccessible tournament. Some have recalled paying roughly $50 for a grounds pass years ago and enjoying an entire day of tennis, moving from court to court without spending a fortune.

Others have questioned whether corporate allocations and influencer attendance have contributed to an atmosphere where ordinary tennis fans are being pushed aside.

One prominent critic called the pricing “actually scandalous,” while another argued that the event is becoming an experience for “the rich and well connected.”

The controversy comes despite uncertainty surrounding two of the sport’s biggest attractions. Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner both withdrew from the Cincinnati Open with injuries, raising questions about their US Open preparations.

Alcaraz , the defending champion, has been sidelined since April but has recently been seen training on hard courts.

Despite those concerns, demand hasn’t appeared to weaken. TicketData’s Keith Pagello said prices continued rising even after both withdrawals.

With the tournament approaching, the debate is now about more than ticket prices and more about whether the US Open is still an event they can realistically afford to experience in person.

articles.title: Serena Williams sends message to Carlos Alcaraz sparking rumors ahead of the US Open
articles.standfirst: Instagram comment revived speculation over a potential partnership
articles.summary: Instagram comment revived speculation over a potential partnership
articles.body:
The biggest question around Carlos Alcaraz had been whether his injured wrist would allow him to return in time for the US Open . Now that he has confirmed his comeback, attention has quickly shifted to whether Serena Williams could be waiting to join him.

Alcaraz announced his return with a social media video and the message, “We’re back, Here we Go.”

Then Williams stepped in. “Ohhhhh ok. I like seeing this,” the 23-time Grand Slam champion commented.

It was only six words, but given the speculation already surrounding the pair, the response was enough to send tennis fans back into detective mode.

Nothing has been officially announced. Still, Williams has previously interacted with Alcaraz ’s recovery posts, and another message linked to the rumors — “They are not ready” — only strengthened the sense that something could be developing behind the scenes.

Why an Alcaraz-Williams team feels possible

The timing works in a way it did not a few weeks ago. Alcaraz has been sidelined since April because of a wrist injury and withdrew from both the French Open and Wimbledon rather than risk worsening the problem.

His absence from Cincinnati created another layer of uncertainty over whether he would even be ready for New York. That changed with his latest announcement.

The US Open mixed doubles tournament is scheduled for August 24-26 and still had wildcard places available in the supplied information.

The event has been deliberately built around star power, with Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka among the high-profile names already linked in teams.

A pairing involving Williams and Alcaraz would fit that philosophy almost perfectly. It would also create one of the biggest attractions of the tournament before the singles draw even begins.

A useful test before singles

The pairing wouldn't be valuable only as a spectacle. Alcaraz hasn't competed in more than four months, meaning the challenge in New York goes well beyond simply being healthy enough to swing a racket again.

The shortened mixed doubles format could give him competitive repetitions without immediately exposing him to the demands of a five-set singles match.

Before the injury, Alcaraz had been in excellent form, winning 22 of 25 matches and claiming titles at the Australian Open and in Doha.

He also enters the US Open with significant ranking pressure. Alcaraz remains No.2 and has 2,000 points to defend, while Jannik Sinner holds a sizeable advantage at the top.

Williams , meanwhile, has already returned to competition this summer and has played doubles alongside Venus Williams , which gives the rumor another layer of plausibility.

Until the remaining mixed doubles teams are officially announced, though, that is all it remains: a rumor. But after Alcaraz confirmed his return and Williams immediately responded, the possibility no longer feels quite so far-fetched.

articles.title: US Open 2026 Tickets: How much are tickets for the US Grand Slam?
articles.standfirst: Fans can still find cheaper options, but premium seats are reaching huge numbers
articles.summary: Fans can still find cheaper options, but premium seats are reaching huge numbers
articles.body:
The US Open has become one of the biggest sporting spectacles in the world, combining elite tennis with New York entertainment, celebrity appearances and a festival-like atmosphere.

However, fans hoping to watch the 2026 Grand Slam in person will face a major question before making plans which is how much will tickets actually cost?

The tournament begins on Tuesday, August 25, at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center , with 128 men and 128 women competing for one of tennis’ most prestigious titles.

Defending champions Carlos Alcaraz and Aryna Sabalenka headline a star-studded field that includes Novak Djokovic, Coco Gauff, Iga Swiatek, Jannik Sinner, Alexander Zverev and Jessica Pegula .

Ticket prices vary significantly depending on the session, stadium and location, with some options remaining accessible while premium seats have reached record levels.

Cheapest US Open 2026 tickets and what fans can expect to pay

Fans looking for the lowest-cost way to attend the tournament can find tickets starting around $49 , including fees, for certain sessions on resale platforms.

Some general admission grounds passes and other events have been listed from around $23, although availability and prices can change as the tournament approaches.

Grounds passes provide access to the wider USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center , allowing fans to watch matches on outside courts and experience the atmosphere around the venue.

However, they don't guarantee entry into Arthur Ashe Stadium , where the biggest matches are played. The biggest price increases have been seen around high-demand sessions.

Some resale listings for opening-week grounds passes have climbed above $360 , despite face-value prices being much lower.

Arthur Ashe Stadium tickets are also commanding premium prices.

Upper-level seats have reached several hundred dollars, while lower sections closer to the court can cost more than $500 . Some premium hospitality and courtside options have reached thousands of dollars.

The increase comes as the US Open continues a major transformation of Arthur Ashe Stadium , with an $800 million renovation project designed to add upgraded seating and hospitality areas.

Why are US Open tickets becoming so expensive?

The rising cost of attending the US Open is linked to several factors, including increased demand for live sports, the popularity of tennis among younger audiences and the growth of the secondary ticket market.

The tournament has become more than just a tennis event, attracting celebrities, athletes and entertainment figures while creating a unique New York experience.

USTA chief commercial officer Kirsten Corio defended the organization’s approach, pointing to efforts such as Fan Week, which allows fans to attend qualifying matches, practices and other events at lower prices.

“You could see Djokovic on Arthur Ashe playing a practice match against another top-10 player for free in the first row,” Corio said. “That’s like no other sport that I can think of.”

The 2026 US Open will also feature special attractions outside the main tournament.

A legends exhibition featuring Roger Federer, John McEnroe, Andre Agassi and Andy Roddick will take place on August 25, while The Lumineers will perform during the tournament’s opening events.

Federer said returning to Arthur Ashe Stadium would be a meaningful experience.

“So many unforgettable moments of my career happened in New York, and Arthur Ashe Stadium is a place that means a great deal to me,” Federer said.

With some cheaper options still available but premium seats becoming increasingly expensive, fans will need to decide how much they are willing to spend to experience one of tennis’ biggest stages.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz can’t hide his admiration for Serena Williams during US Open return
articles.summary: No matter that Carlos Alcaraz is one of the best players in the world today, sharing the court with Serena Williams is still a special experience for the Spaniard.
articles.body:
No matter that Carlos Alcaraz is one of the best players in the world today, sharing the court with Serena Williams is still a special experience for the Spaniard.

During an interview, Alcaraz appeared almost in disbelief as he talked about playing doubles alongside the tennis legend at the US Open.

Both stars are making their return to the court and were among the most cheered players of the event. You do not always get the chance to play alongside a legend, and Alcaraz is clearly making the most of the opportunity.

Back in action, he is enjoying the moment, having fun, learning and, above all, showing his admiration for Serena.

articles.title: Serena and Venus Williams receive a last-minute wild card to play doubles at the U.S. Open
articles.standfirst: Tennis icons reunite at Flushing Meadows after an emotional comeback to doubles
articles.summary: Tennis icons reunite at Flushing Meadows after an emotional comeback to doubles
articles.body:
S erena and Venus Williams are heading back to the U.S. Open together, with the legendary sisters receiving a late invitation to compete in the women’s doubles draw at the 2026 tournament.

The United States Tennis Association confirmed Wednesday, Aug. 26, that the Williams sisters had been awarded a wild card.

The decision gives fans another opportunity to watch one of the most successful doubles partnerships in tennis history compete together on one of the sport’s biggest stages.

“ Serena and Venus Williams will receive a wild card entry into the 2026 US Open Women’s Doubles Championship, as the USTA announced US Open women’s and men’s doubles wild cards today,” the United States Tennis Association (USTA) said in a statement.

The announcement comes after a dramatic few months for Serena , who returned to Grand Slam singles competition this summer following a lengthy absence. The younger Williams sister had not played a Grand Slam singles match since 2022 before entering Wimbledon this year.

Her return to competitive tennis also included plans to reunite with Venus in doubles. Those plans were derailed when Serena suffered a knee injury during her singles campaign and subsequently withdrew from their scheduled doubles appearance.

Serena expressed her disappointment at missing the opportunity to play alongside her sister.

“Coming back to compete again has been a gift, and the opportunity to play alongside Venus once more meant the world to me. I did everything I could to be ready, but unfortunately my knee just isn’t ready to compete.”

The sisters ultimately got another chance to test themselves together at the Cincinnati Open on Aug. 17. It was their first doubles match as a team since 2022, although the comeback ended in the opening round when they were defeated by Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns.

Now, their return to New York gives them a chance to build on that experience.

The Williams sisters are chasing another chapter in New York

The U.S. Open holds particular significance for Serena and Venus because their doubles record at the tournament is already part of their remarkable legacy.

The pair have captured the women's doubles championship at Flushing Meadows twice, winning in 1999 and again in 2009. Across the four Grand Slam tournaments, they have accumulated 14 women's doubles titles, including those two U.S. Open victories.

Their success was built on an unusual combination of athleticism, power and understanding developed over decades of playing together.

Their doubles partnership also became one of the defining features of the Williams sisters' careers, even as both established extraordinary individual records in singles.

Their 2026 appearance, however, arrives under very different circumstances.

Venus , 46, and Serena , who turns 45 in September, are no longer regular fixtures on the Grand Slam circuit.

Serena's return this season has therefore attracted considerable attention, while Venus has continued to make her own comeback attempts after dealing with injuries and extended periods away from competition.

For Serena, the U.S. Open will provide another opportunity to compete at an event that has played such an important role in her career. She won the singles title in New York six times, while Venus lifted the singles trophy twice.

The doubles wild card also means their reunion will take place in front of a home crowd that has watched the sisters transform women's tennis over several generations.

Their Cincinnati result showed that the pair will have work to do if they are to make a deep run. Nevertheless, the opportunity itself represents a significant moment.

After Wimbledon disappointment and a first-round loss in Cincinnati, the sisters now have another chance to share the court at a Grand Slam.

For tennis fans, it is an unexpected opportunity to see one of the sport's most iconic partnerships together once again. At the U.S. Open, Serena and Venus will attempt to add another chapter to a doubles story that began more than two decades ago.

Their doubles partnership also became one of the defining features of the Williams sisters' careers, even as both established extraordinary individual records in singles.
Their 2026 appearance, however, arrives under very different circumstances.
Venus , 46, and Serena , who turns 45 in September, are no longer regular fixtures on the Grand Slam circuit.

Serena's return this season has therefore attracted considerable attention, while Venus has continued to make her own comeback attempts after dealing with injuries and extended periods away from competition.

For Serena, the U.S. Open will provide another opportunity to compete at an event that has played such an important role in her career. She won the singles title in New York six times, while Venus lifted the singles trophy twice.
The doubles wild card also means their reunion will take place in front of a home crowd that has watched the sisters transform women's tennis over several generations.
Their Cincinnati result showed that the pair will have work to do if they are to make a deep run. Nevertheless, the opportunity itself represents a significant moment.
After Wimbledon disappointment and a first-round loss in Cincinnati, the sisters now have another chance to share the court at a Grand Slam.

For tennis fans, it is an unexpected opportunity to see one of the sport's most iconic partnerships together once again. At the U.S. Open, Serena and Venus will attempt to add another chapter to a doubles story that began more than two decades ago.

Three tennis players, Elena Rybakina, Jessica Pegula and Coco Gauff, want to take advantage of the WTA's current disarray. The domination of Aryna Sabalenka and Iga Swiatek is over, and Rybakina, Pegula and Gauff are in with a chance of snatching the world number one ranking from Sabalenka . Elena is in cotton wool and has not even secured her place in the first round against the unknown Thea Frodin , world No. 580. Sabalenka, Pegula and Gauff's chances depend on winning the title.

articles.title: Djokovic, devastated and in tears from the pain, loses in the first round of the US Open against Navone: "I suffered"
articles.standfirst: The Serbian had not lost in the first round of a "major" since the 2006 Australian Open, more than 20 years ago.
articles.summary: The Serbian had not lost in the first round of a "major" since the 2006 Australian Open, more than 20 years ago.
articles.body:
The Argentine Mariano Navone (25 years old) pulled off a major upset by defeating Novak Djokovic , who made 70 unforced errors, ended up exhausted from vomiting and had to hold back tears at some stages of the match because of the pain , in the first round of the US Open .

I’m really trying to come to terms with what’s happening and see how far I can go like this

The world No. 49 defeated No. 5 7-6(5), 5-7, 4-6, 6-2 and 6-1 at the Arthur Ashe Stadium in a match that lasted 4 hours and 36 minutes.

I suffered throughout the whole match from the fourth game on. Again, I don't want to take anything away from his victory. Congratulations to him. He's a good guy, a fighter. But I didn't enjoy it

Djokovic, 39 years old, a four-time US Open champion and winner of 24 "majors," was playing this tournament for the twentieth time in his career and had a 37-0 record in the first two rounds in New York .

The Serb had not lost in the first round of a "major" since the 2006 Australian Open , more than 20 years ago.

I've been very proud of all the achievements of the past, but the present is the present. I've just come off the court and I'm still trying to manage my body

"The lead-up was tough because I was going to play against the GOAT, against this rival, he has always been on this court (the New York center court). It's a dream. Now I have to recover, I have to go to sleep and get ready," Navone said after the match.

Djokovic's tears during his defeat against Navone

Djokovic, who is still unable to claim his 25th Grand Slam, vomited several times and needed medical attention

During the first 30 minutes Djokovic looked like a player ready to quickly dispatch the world No. 49, taking an early 3-0 and 4-1 lead in the first set, before falling apart.

Djokovic vomited several times during the match , was treated by the physiotherapist after requesting a medical timeout upon losing the fourth set, and then struggled to hold back tears when Navone went 4-1 up in the निर्णत set.

Djokovic's 25th Grand Slam, for which he was seen taking pills to try to recover, will have to keep waiting.

The match ended when an exhausted Djokovic hit a weak return to Navone that the Argentine answered without the Serbian being able to do anything to prevent it.

' Djokovic had already suffered vomiting previously , during his second-round defeat to Thiago Agustín Tirante in Cincinnati. '

'Djokovic: "It’s something I’ve been dealing with this year: vomiting, nausea, a serious problem in that regard"'

Novak Djokovic admitted, after losing to Navone, that he has been dealing with "practically in every match" he has played this year with "vomiting and nausea" and that it is "a serious problem" that makes him unsure how far he can "go."

"I think it was obvious that on the court I had a horrible feeling. It is something that, unfortunately, I have been carrying practically in every match this year: vomiting, nausea, a serious problem in that regard. Afterwards, my whole body basically starts to break down with cramps and pain. In the end, my back and shoulder could not take any more, and I couldn't close it out," Djokovic said at the post-match press conference in statements reported by the EFE agency.

"I had a break lead in the fourth set, but I suffered throughout the match from the fourth game on. Again, I don't want to take anything away from his victory. Congratulations to him. He's a good guy, a fighter. But I didn't enjoy it," he added.

'Djokovic had never lost in the first round in his 19 US Opens: "Yes, it's a good record, another one. But, yes, the truth is I'm not thinking too much about it. Of course, I've been very proud of all the achievements of the past, but the present is the present. I just came off the court and I'm still trying to manage my body".'

"Right now I'm not going that deep. I'm just really trying to cope with what's happening and see how far I can go like this," he added.

Since his debut in the majors, he has never failed to reach the second round. That makes 21 in a row, closing in on the Open Era record of his idol Rafael Nadal, with 34 .

Safiullin also came out wearing a sleeve on his right arm, the same one the seven-time major champion has been using since he withdrew from the Cincinnati Masters 1000. It gives him greater confidence in his shot-making.

The Podolsk-born tennis player had a point for 3-0 . But the balance of his unforced errors was greater than that of his winners. He does not distinguish between hitting hard and keeping it in.

Another winning forehand from the world number three gave him the third break . Fist raised. With the machine well-oiled, he accelerated toward victory. The organization closed the center court's retractable roof due to the threat of rain.

articles.title: Aryna Sabalenka fires back at critics of her US Open outfit: ‘Who cares what people think?’
articles.standfirst: The reaction was more amusing than upsetting for the Belarusian star
articles.summary: The reaction was more amusing than upsetting for the Belarusian star
articles.body:
A ryna Sabalenka's US Open wardrobe has generated almost as much conversation as her tennis this week, but the world's top-ranked player made it clear that public opinion is not going to influence her fashion choices. After some fans on social media criticized the outfit she wore during her mixed doubles appearance at Flushing Meadows, Sabalenka responded with a message that reflected the confidence that has helped her become one of the sport's dominant players.

“Who cares what people think?” Sabalenka said during Friday's media day. “I love it.” The comments came after the Belarusian star drew attention for a black mesh Nike dress that revealed an electric orange sports bra and matching briefs underneath. The outfit became a topic of debate online, with some fans praising its boldness.

The reaction was more amusing than upsetting, according to Sabalenka. “I love basically everything about my outfit,” she said. “I love that it’s different. I love that this outfit is bold. Whatever people saying on internet, I heard they probably didn’t like it … it’s funny for me.”

A tennis Star Embracing a Different Kind of Spotlight

Professional tennis has long balanced tradition with innovation, and player fashion has often become part of that conversation. From Serena Williams' iconic outfits to Andre Agassi's colorful looks in the 1990s, some of the sport's biggest stars have used apparel to express personality as much as performance.

Sabalenka's latest look appears to fit into that category. Rather than viewing the outfit as a controversial choice, she sees it as part of a larger creative concept that Nike has developed throughout the Grand Slam season. According to the tennis star, each major tournament this year has featured a different theme.

“Surfing for the Australian Open, ballet for Roland Garros, cricket for Wimbledon, ” she explained. “Now it’s basketball and we’re in New York . Isn’t it the perfect fit?” The basketball inspiration is particularly fitting given New York City's deep connection to the sport. While tennis remains the focus at the US Open, Sabalenka embraced a design that attempted to capture some of the city's broader sporting culture.

Criticism comes with every outfit

One of the more interesting parts of Sabalenka's response was her suggestion that criticism is unavoidable regardless of what athletes wear.

She argued that fans complained when Nike produced safer, more traditional designs and are now complaining again when the company pushes creative boundaries.

“When Nike was pretty simple and standard, they were complaining,” she said. “When Nike went really cool and fun and trying to get back, they always complain.”

Her comments highlight a reality faced by many modern athletes. Social media has created an environment where every aspect of a player's appearance, performance and personality can become a topic of instant public discussion.

articles.title: Novak Djokovic's dead giveaway for his tennis future became clear at the U.S. Open
articles.standfirst: Father Time looks to be finally catching up to the legendary tennis player.
articles.summary: Father Time looks to be finally catching up to the legendary tennis player.
articles.body:
The first round of the U.S. Open provided one of the most stunning upsets in recent memory. The legendary Novak Djokovic couldn't get rid of 25-year-old Argentinian Mariano Navone , who outlasted Djokovic and came away victorious.

The caveat, of course, is that Djokovic was not physically well . He was spotted vomiting multiple times throughout the match , which undoubtedly affected his play. But aside from his body betraying him on that specific day, the end of the match may have proved more telling than anything else.

Djokovic simply couldn't hold back the tears after Navone notched the match-winning point. For a player who is always so even-keeled and serious, seeing Djokovic cry had many wondering if this is truly the beginning of the end for a true icon of the sport .

Novak Djokovic may have to ponder retirement due to his health

As it turns out, his health may actually be the reason those tears came out . Djokovic admitted after the loss that Father Time could very well be finally catching up to him.

I didn’t enjoy myself. I think it was obvious that it was an awful feeling on the court for me. It’s something that I’ve been carrying, unfortunately, pretty much every match this year: vomiting, throwing up, a serious issue there. Then my whole body starts to collapse, basically cramping and pain. Yeah, the back just gave up in the end and shoulder.

Djokovic had revealed in early August that an underlying health issue rears its ugly head particularly in hot and humid environments . Of course, those types of conditions are common during the tennis season. Djokovic will seriously have to consider if it's time to hang it all up sooner than later, for the sake of his health.

articles.standfirst: Her outfits have become part of the show long before the first serve
articles.summary: Her outfits have become part of the show long before the first serve
articles.body:
Naomi Osaka and Zendaya have something in common: both use clothing as a form of expression, but they also give every piece a purpose.

Osaka is changing the way tennis is seen, as people are now waiting to see what iconic outfit she will wear when she arrives at the court.

Fashion and tennis are becoming part of the same conversation

Many may think sports and fashion do not go hand in hand. But Osaka is rewriting the way clothing can become a form of self-expression , help you feel more confident on the court and, above all, allow you to be yourself in a world where too much is expected of you.

This time at the US Open, Osaka surprised once again with the outfit she chose . The crowd rose to welcome her and, above all, support her. It was not only about the clothing, but also the way she styled her hair . Naomi did not miss a detail, r epresenting American culture through a fashion icon who inspired her.

The spectacular jellyfish outfit at the Australian Open, the sparkly Eiffel Tower-inspired golden dress at the French Open and the elegant all-white Japanese kimono at Wimbledon were each designed for the occasion. They proved Osaka knows how to make a grand entrance at the Grand Slams, and her arrival at this year's US Open was always going to turn heads.

This time, the outfit told her story

The four-time major champion walked onto the court for her first-round match against Russia's Anastasia Zakharova in New York wearing a hooded white gown covered with newspaper headlines highlighting key moments from her career.

Underneath, Osaka wore an all-black basketball-style kit , which she used as she fought her way to a 7-6 (8-6), 7-6 (7-3) win over world No. 101 Zakharova.

Osaka revealed that the look was inspired by NBA legend Allen Iverson , whose influence helped reshape the way athletes approached fashion during the late 1990s and early 2000s.

For Osaka, Iverson represents more than style . She sees him as a trailblazer who changed how NBA players dress and helped open the conversation around self-expression through fashion in sports.

articles.summary: Serena is back on the court, and her fashion statements are back with her
articles.body:
Serena Williams is already a veteran of tennis. However, that does not mean she goes unnoticed at the US Open. Quite the opposite. She is not only a player looking to compete in the tournament, but also a major sports celebrity who draws attention even during a training session.

The return of the Williams sisters to US Open doubles has fans talking. Serena and Venus Williams are drawn to face Maya Joint and Chan Hao-Ching in women’s doubles. But beyond Serena returning to the sport alongside her sister, her daring outfits have also made their comeback.

Serena is making her return on her own terms

With Nike once again by her side, Serena showed off two looks that align with the way she has approached fashion throughout her career. This time, she is embracing her curves and deliberately putting them on display . One pair of leggings fully exposed her right leg, highlighting the strength she has built through years of training , while another outfit was sheer, revealing the results of the work she continues to put in at the gym.

Serena is stepping back into tennis with what appears to be less pressure than when she was fully committed to the sport and competing in her prime. Now, it seems she is returning to have fun and rediscover what she loves about the game, with different goals and fewer expectations surrounding her comeback.

Her clothes still carry a message of freedom and self-expression

That purpose, however, appears unchanged. The body Serena embraces is the same one that carries her and gets her through every day . The dimensions do not matter when it comes to what she chooses to wear or how she wants to express herself through fashion.

Now, Serena also appears ready to step back into the fashion conversation , potentially setting up a style competition with Naomi Osaka over who can make the biggest statement on the court and what each of them wants their outfits to say.

articles.title: Sabalenka argues with a journalist who asked about her parties: "You are a joke... Think before you speak"
articles.standfirst: Moments of tension at the US Open during Aryna Sabalenka's press conference after defeating Polina Iatcenko
articles.summary: Moments of tension at the US Open during Aryna Sabalenka's press conference after defeating Polina Iatcenko
articles.body:
Aryna Sabalenka abruptly cut off questions about her private life and pre-US Open activities.

The Belarusian tennis player had a very tense and uncomfortable exchange of words with a journalist at the press conference following her 6-1, 6-1 victory over Polina Iatcenko .

"Parties, fun... I mean, why would you say something like that? Why would it even occur to you to think about that? What kind of question is that? "}

The journalist asked Sabalenka about her parties , and Aryna's response was forceful.

Sabalenka, who has more than 5.6 million followers on Instagram and usually posts content on social media about the various events she attends and the brands she collaborates with, replied: "You are a joke..." .

Ah, sure, before I didn't take things seriously. Next question. Think before you speak

"Parties, having fun... I mean, why would you say something like that? Why would it even occur to you to think that? What kind of question is that? "Just because I posted, let's say, some activities with brands, you think I've been partying instead of training? That question... where is it coming from?" she protested.

'When the journalist tried to justify himself, the tennis player reacted annoyed: "Ah, right, before I didn’t take things seriously. Next question. Think before you speak".'

articles.title: The US Open’s Honey Deuce is a $17 million tradition with a massive supply chain
articles.standfirst: How a simple vodka cocktail became one of the most recognizable symbols of tennis in New York
articles.summary: How a simple vodka cocktail became one of the most recognizable symbols of tennis in New York
articles.body:
At the US Open , the biggest stars aren't the only ones drawing attention.

Every summer, thousands of fans arrive at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center looking for the same thing: a clear commemorative cup filled with a pink cocktail and topped by three green melon balls.

The Honey Deuce has become as closely associated with the US Open as packed sessions at Arthur Ashe Stadium, late-summer heat and the tournament's electric New York atmosphere. What looks like a simple courtside drink, however, requires months of preparation and an enormous agricultural operation.

The numbers tell the story.

In 2025, fans bought 738,459 Honey Deuces , producing more than $17 million in sales. For the 2026 tournament, roughly 8,000 cases of honeydew melons will travel from California to Queens, filling eight semi-trucks along the way.

Jared Walton , director of national accounts for Baldor Specialty Foods, starts thinking about those melons every spring. That's when he contacts Turlock Fruit Company in California to determine how much honeydew the US Open will need months before the tournament begins.

"I feel like people think honeydew balls show up in Queens every summer," Walton laughs. "And it just magically happens. But there's extensive planning."

The fruit eventually arrives in New York, where workers turn it into the cocktail's signature garnish. The operation has become a remarkable behind-the-scenes part of the tournament.

The melon balls measure roughly 1.57 inches across and come three to a skewer, creating the visual effect of miniature tennis balls. With 800,000 commemorative cups ordered for 2026, the tournament expects to need more than 2.4 million melon balls.

And there is no machine doing the work.

The melon balls must come from workers using handheld scoopers. Baldor orders roughly 500 melon ballers for the operation, while a team of more than 20 employees can begin work as early as 5:45 a.m.

"It's actually somewhat magical seeing them take a big, round sphere and turn it into multiple mini round spheres," Walton says.

The logistics become even more complicated because the melon balls have a shelf life of only about five days. Baldor has added a refrigerated trailer at the tournament to help maintain the supply throughout the event.

From Kentucky Derby inspiration to US Open icon

The Honey Deuce traces its origins to 2006, when Grey Goose asked restaurateur and mixologist Nick Mautone to create a signature cocktail for the US Open. The drink debuted at the tournament in 2007.

Mautone already had a connection to tennis. In his early 20s, he worked at the US Open, hauling ice and working as a barback. Years later, while preparing a summer fruit salad after returning from a Long Island farmers market, he noticed something familiar in the honeydew.

"It was divine inspiration, like 'Oh my god, this looks like a tennis ball," he says.

That observation became the foundation of the drink.

Mautone experimented with five or six versions before settling on the combination that fans now recognize: Grey Goose vodka, lemonade and raspberry liqueur, finished with the three honeydew balls.

The simplicity was intentional. A drink served to tens of thousands of people couldn't rely on complicated techniques or an elaborate ingredient list.

"We knew we were going to sell a lot, so we had to simplify the recipe and make it something that could work for everybody," says Mautone , creator of the Honey Deuce.

The name also fits perfectly. "Deuce" refers to a 40-40 tie in tennis, while the honeydew provides the drink's signature ingredient.

Mautone initially considered other names, including "30 Love," while another version called the "Courtside" featured rosemary citrus syrup, fresh lemon juice, vodka and raspberry liqueur. But the Honey Deuce's straightforward formula ultimately won.

Its rise also had a major influence from the tournament itself.

Daniel Zausner , COO at the USTA National Tennis Center, wanted the US Open to develop a signature drink after seeing the way spectators embraced the mint julep at the Kentucky Derby. The julep wasn't simply something people drank; it became part of the experience and something fans wanted to take home.

"You see all the imagery of women in their stiletto heels, with the large-brim hats and their dresses. Women were walking around with stacks of these glasses," Zausner says of his experience at Churchill Downs. "It meant so much to them to take home four, six glasses, whatever it might be."

That idea helped shape the Honey Deuce into something bigger than a concession item.

"I stole it from the Derby," Zausner says.

The USTA then moved quickly to secure a vodka partner.

"Literally the first call I made that Monday morning was to someone on our sponsorship team," Zausner says. "I said, 'We need a vodka sponsor and we need one tomorrow."

Grey Goose became that partner, and the relationship has continued for nearly two decades. The USTA and Grey Goose first partnered in 2007, with the brand becoming the tournament's official vodka and the Honey Deuce emerging as its signature cocktail.

The drink's growth has been extraordinary.

The US Open sold only about 24,000 Honey Deuces in its debut year at $12 apiece. By 2025, sales had climbed beyond 738,000 at $23 each. Grey Goose says more than 3.5 million Honey Deuces have been sold since 2011.

The rise mirrors the tournament's growing attendance and increasingly social atmosphere. The US Open surpassed 1 million spectators for the second straight year in 2025, giving the cocktail an enormous audience.

The Honey Deuce also benefits from something few other sports drinks can replicate: instant visual recognition.

A fan holding the distinctive cup doesn't need to explain where they are. The three melon balls, pink drink and US Open branding do the work.

"People come through the gates every morning and besides asking 'How do you find this court to find a player practice,' the most asked question is 'Where's the nearest Grey Goose cup?'" Zausner says. "They just want to get a Honey Deuce , take a picture with it, let the whole world know they're at the US Open."

That social-media appeal helped turn the cocktail into a piece of tournament culture. Taylor Swift, Kendall Jenner, Timothée Chalamet and Leonardo DiCaprio have all been photographed with the drink, while Mautone points to Bruce Springsteen's Honey Deuce as a personal highlight.

"Seeing Bruce Springsteen last year drinking a Honey Deuce, that was the pinnacle for me," Mautone laughs.

Aleco Azqueta , global vice president of marketing at Grey Goose, describes the cocktail's success as an "overnight success 19 years in the making."

The commemorative cup has become almost as important as the drink itself. Each cup features the names of previous US Open champions, giving fans a souvenir after the cocktail disappears. Some collectors stack the cups several feet high, while resale listings can push individual cups into the $10-to-$20 range.

The US Open has leaned into that demand, selling Honey Deuce-themed shirts, hats, towels, candles and even a branded melon baller.

The result is a rare sports tradition that lives simultaneously at the concession stand, on social media and in fans' homes.

And behind every photograph sits a supply chain that began months earlier in California.

"Everyone wants that picture with the cup saying, 'I got it this year,'" Walton says.

articles.title: Trinity Rodman turns heads at the U.S. Open with her outfit to support her boyfriend, Ben Shelton
articles.standfirst: The USWNT star made her feelings clear as Shelton battled through a four-set thriller at Arthur Ashe Stadium
articles.summary: The USWNT star made her feelings clear as Shelton battled through a four-set thriller at Arthur Ashe Stadium
articles.body:
T rinity Rodman made sure there was no confusion about who she was rooting for at the U.S. Open.

The Washington Spirit and U.S. women's national team star turned up at Arthur Ashe Stadium on Wednesday to watch boyfriend Ben Shelton take on Hubert Hurkacz , and her outfit quickly became one of the most talked-about moments surrounding the match.

Rodman wore a black crop top carrying a simple but unmistakable message: “I ❤️ my boyfriend.”

The shirt immediately caught attention as cameras repeatedly showed Rodman in the stands while Shelton battled Poland's Hurkacz in the second round.

The 24-year-old soccer star has become a familiar face at Shelton's matches, but Wednesday's outfit took her public support to another level.

Rodman had already attended Shelton's first-round match earlier in the week. For that appearance, she wore a colorful shirt while cheering on the American tennis star as he defeated Tallon Griekspoor. This time, there was no need to guess what Rodman was thinking.

Her appearance also came in the middle of the NWSL season. Rodman's Washington Spirit had played Bay FC on Sunday, and she was scheduled to return to action against the Portland Thorns on Sunday.

That gives her roughly a week between competitive matches, creating an opportunity to spend time in New York and support Shelton during one of tennis' biggest tournaments.

The Spirit are still expected to train during the week, but Rodman has clearly found a way to balance her soccer responsibilities with following Shelton's run in Flushing Meadows. And Shelton gave her plenty to celebrate.

Shelton survives Hurkacz and keeps his US Open run alive

The No. 8-seeded American entered the tournament carrying significant expectations. Shelton is one of the country's leading men's tennis players and has reached the US Open semifinals before, making him one of the strongest American hopes for a deep run. He delivered another important win Wednesday.

Shelton defeated Hurkacz 6-3, 5-7, 7-6(3), 7-5 to reach the third round, surviving a match between two of the biggest servers in the draw. The contest lasted three hours, with both players trading powerful serves and lengthy rallies before Shelton finally broke through in the fourth set.

The victory keeps Shelton's hopes of becoming the first American man to win a Grand Slam singles title since 2003 alive.

That possibility has become a particularly intriguing storyline at this year's US Open. Jannik Sinner withdrew because of injury, while defending champion Carlos Alcaraz entered the tournament after spending roughly four and a half months away from competition because of a wrist problem.

With several major contenders dealing with injuries or questions about their form, Shelton has an opportunity to make a serious push. His path will continue Friday, when he faces Canada's Denis Shapovalov in the third round.

For Rodman , Wednesday's trip to Queens was about more than simply watching a tennis match.

Her relationship with Shelton has been public since 2025, when the pair began drawing attention through social media. Rodman previously explained that she initially reached out to Shelton herself, turning an online interaction into a relationship that quickly became public.

The two have also made a point of supporting each other's careers. Shelton has attended Rodman's soccer matches, including her appearance at the National Bank Open last year, while Rodman has regularly appeared courtside during Shelton's tournaments.

That mutual support has made them one of the more recognizable young sports couples in the United States, with both competing at the highest levels of their respective sports. Their timing is also notable.

articles.title: Influencers interrupt Naomi Osaka’s US Open match to stage photo shoot in luxury suite
articles.summary: Naomi Osaka was ready to serve. Anastasia Zakharova was waiting on the other side of the net. But before the match could continue, chair umpire Kader Nouni had to turn his attention away from the court.
articles.body:
Naomi Osaka was ready to serve. Anastasia Zakharova was waiting on the other side of the net. But before the match could continue, chair umpire Kader Nouni had to turn his attention away from the court.

A group inside a luxury suite was standing, making noise and recording content. Another woman was seen using a bright ring light while play was taking place inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.

Nouni finally intervened and asked them to sit down. For a few uncomfortable seconds, the tennis had to wait while the group finished turning one of the sport’s biggest stages into its own photo studio.

Thousands of fans would have loved the chance to be inside that stadium. These guests had one of the best views in the building, but at that moment, watching the match appeared to be the last thing on their minds.
